note: An inline chain endpoint 45.000 m from its arc under the model SPEC 3.3.3 states, which a conforming reader must accept. THIS CASE CATCHES A MODEL THAT OVER-READS: a reader taking the cosine of each segment's START latitude reads this endpoint at 67.409 m and wrongly refuses a legal document; flat degrees-times-111320 reads 117.723 m and Web Mercator 117.591 m, and both wrongly refuse it too. THE THIRTEEN DEGREES OF LATITUDE ARE DELIBERATE AND ARE NOT A TRAIL. The effect being pinned is a percentage error, so a realistic arc hides it: an earlier version of this case used three degrees, where the segment-start model reads 48.842 m against a 50 m tolerance - the number moved and the verdict did not, and a corpus case is a verdict, so it discriminated against nothing. THE ARC IS A MERIDIAN so the projected segment is vertical in every model and the distance is exactly the longitude offset times whatever scale the model uses; no model can disagree about the arithmetic, only about the scale, which is the thing under test. See diagnose/inline-endpoint-beyond-tolerance.vnx, whose arc runs the other way for a reason.
